Intriguingly, we establish fast mixing of these classical Markov chains using tools from quantum physics like Lieb-Robinson bounds.

title: Contractions of realizations and differential invariants of the algebra sl(2,C)
summary: In this paper, we formalize a method for constructing limit transitions between local realizations of Lie algebras based on contractions of the corresponding algebras. In the complex holomorphic category, contractions of faithful realizations of the special linear algebra sl(2, C) to the complex three-dimensional Poincaré algebra and the Weyl-Heisenberg algebra are explicitly constructed. For the contraction of a generating realization of the algebra sl(2,C) to the algebra g_{3.4}^{-1}, differential invariants are constructed and a limit system of Newtonian type is found.

title: Controlled Magnon Chirality and Its Reversal by Anisotropy in Altermagnetic FeF$_2$
summary: In altermagnets, the exchange symmetry of two mutually compensating magnetic sublattices permits spin-polarized electronic bands and chirality-split magnon bands. Because these effects have opposite signs in domains related by time reversal, magnetic-domain control is essential for their observation and utilization. Using half-polarized neutron diffraction, we demonstrate that we can control magnetic domain imbalance in a single crystal of FeF$_2$ by field cooling, and we relate this response to the established piezomagnetism in this material. Our half-polarized inelastic neutron scattering measurements directly resolve the altermagnetic splitting of chiral magnon bands. Strikingly, we observe a clear reversal of chirality near $\mathbf{Q}=(0.5,0.5,1)$, where the altermagnetic exchange splitting vanishes and no chirality is expected in a nonrelativistic exchange model. This reversal of the chirality is well explained by the presence of a transverse component of the single-ion anisotropy tensor, which rotates between Fe sublattices related by the crystal's altermagnetic $4_2$ screw symmetry. These results allow us to resolve fine features of the spin Hamiltonian for FeF$_2$ and show how symmetry-governed relativistic anisotropy can reshape altermagnetic spin dynamics, as well as providing an avenue for control of magnetic domains and the net chiral response.

title: Electric Fields Turn Vacancy-trapping Grain Boundaries into Li-Ion Pathways in Li2O
summary: Ion transport in solids has conventionally been understood from equilibrium diffusion, yet ions in batteries are driven by electric fields. Does field-driven ion transport follow equilibrium behavior? We examined this question in bulk Li2O and at its grain boundaries (GBs) using electric-field molecular dynamics combining a machine learning interatomic potential with a Bader charge prediction model. Although Li diffusion in cubic Li2O is isotropic at zero field, an electric field renders it orientation dependent because Li hops along a limited set of crystallographic pathways that the field biases unequally. At GBs, this anisotropy becomes a qualitative difference: a GB that strongly traps Li vacancies but exhibits a strong field response releases them under a field, whereas a weakly responsive GB retains them despite weaker vacancy trapping. These results show that field-driven GB transport is governed not by static thermodynamics alone but by the angle between the electric field and the diffusion pathways of the constituent grains.

title: Magic of Dicke states: density, cost and yield
summary: Dicke states are an elementary family of many-body quantum states, consisting of equal superpositions of all configurations of $L$ qubits with $n$ excitations. We show that their magic, as measured by the stabilizer Rényi entropy (SRE), is extensive at every filling $f=n/L$ except half-filling, and we obtain the magic density analytically, together with the subleading terms. In the context of fault-tolerant quantum computation, we also investigate the yield of Dicke states, and find that they can produce on average an extensive number of CCZ states (or $T$ states with a catalyst) at any $0<f<1$. This yield is not self-averaging, but fluctuates from run to run by $O(L)$, as if it were set by a hidden phase shared by all qubits. At half-filling, the SRE grows only logarithmically, while the preparation cost, average yield and relative entropy of magic remain extensive, so that a small SRE does not necessarily signal a weak resource. These results can be understood by viewing the Dicke state as a fixed-magnetization projection of a product of tilted spins.

title: Low-Temperature Heat Capacity of Single-Walled Carbon Nanotube Bundles with low dimensional gas systems
summary: Low-temperature heat-capacity data for pristine single-walled carbon nanotube (SWCNT) bundles and for SWCNT/gas systems containing adsorbed Xe, Ne, N2, and CH4 were analyzed within a phenomenological framework. The data were fitted within the phenomenological form C(T) = C3T3 + C5T5, where the coefficients are interpreted as effective parameters of the coupled SWCNT-adsorbate excitation spectrum. Pristine SWCNT bundles exhibit a negative C5 coefficient, reflecting a non-Debye dispersive contribution associated with low-energy flexural-like modes. Gas adsorption systematically modifies both C3 and C5, indicating that the adsorbate's heat-capacity contribution may not be treated as fully independent. The Xe series suggests that mass loading, modified adsorbate-nanotube interaction, and changes in intertube coupling slightly reshape the nanotube vibrational response. Coverage-dependent measurements for Ne reveal a progressive shift from nanotube-dominated excitations toward domination of additional low-energy adsorbate modes in the phonon spectrum of the SWCNT-Ne system, while molecular adsorbates (N2, CH4) introduce translational, librational, orientational, and rotational degrees of freedom that generate correspondingly stronger perturbations.

title: Magic of Dicke states: density, cost and yield
summary: Dicke states are an elementary family of many-body quantum states, consisting of equal superpositions of all configurations of $L$ qubits with $n$ excitations. We show that their magic, as measured by the stabilizer Rényi entropy (SRE), is extensive at every filling $f=n/L$ except half-filling, and we obtain the magic density analytically, together with the subleading terms. In the context of fault-tolerant quantum computation, we also investigate the yield of Dicke states, and find that they can produce on average an extensive number of CCZ states (or $T$ states with a catalyst) at any $0<f<1$. This yield is not self-averaging, but fluctuates from run to run by $O(L)$, as if it were set by a hidden phase shared by all qubits. At half-filling, the SRE grows only logarithmically, while the preparation cost, average yield and relative entropy of magic remain extensive, so that a small SRE does not necessarily signal a weak resource. These results can be understood by viewing the Dicke state as a fixed-magnetization projection of a product of tilted spins.

title: Projection of massive and interacting conformal theories to the future null infinity
summary: On a four-dimensional, globally hyperbolic and asymptotically flat spacetime, we consider a real, linear, massive scalar field. Within the framework of perturbative algebraic quantum field theory and inspired by the principle of perturbative agreement, we regard the mass term in the underlying Lagrangian as an interaction potential. This allows us to construct the algebra of observables of the massive theory and, using a Møller map, to represent its elements as formal power series in the squared mass, with coefficients in the algebra of observables of a massless, conformally coupled scalar field. Following [DMP06], we use the bulk-to-boundary correspondence for the massless theory to project each coefficient to future null infinity $\mathscr{I}^+$.In four-dimensional Minkowski spacetime, we prove convergence of the projected series in the presence of an infrared cut-off and show that the global adiabatic limit exists but is trivial. We circumvent this obstruction by exploiting the time-slice axiom, which allows us to restrict our attention to observables localized in a causally convex neighbourhood containing a Cauchy hypersurface. Removing the cut-off locally yields a non-trivial limit and hence a bulk-to-boundary correspondence for the massive theory. We then extend our procedure to a self-interacting real scalar field. We represent interacting observables as formal power series in the coupling constant, with coefficients in the algebra of observables of a massless, conformally coupled scalar field. Each coefficient in the domain of the bulk-to-boundary map can thus be projected to future null infinity. As a concrete example, we apply this method to the stress-energy tensor of a massless scalar field with a quartic self-interaction, computing its projection up to first order in perturbation theory.

title: Thermally Hysteretic Room-Temperature Nonlinear Hall Effect in Bulk EuTe4
comment: 21 pages, 4 figures in the main text, 6 figures and 1 table in supplemental material
summary: The nonlinear Hall effect (NLHE) is a novel transport phenomena and shows great potential applications of future electronics. However, the realization of a giant and tunable NLHE in bulk materials at room temperature remains elusive. Here, we report a NLHE in bulk EuTe4 single crystals, which persists up to 400 K and exhibits pronounced thermal hysteresis behaviors. The ratio of nonlinear Hall voltages during warming and cooling processes is about 4.7 at 340 K. Such phenomena could be related to the inversion-symmetry-broken charge density wave state in EuTe4. These findings demonstrate bulk EuTe$_4$ as a promising platform for tunable nonlinear electronic devices at room temperature.

title: Pressure-driven evolution of crystal and molecular structures reshapes excited-state competition in coronene
summary: Molecular nanocarbons exhibit unique optoelectronic properties and considered as promising candidates for organic device applications, however, understanding how molecular geometry and crystal packing jointly govern physical properties remains a fundamental challenge in π-conjugated molecular materials. Here, we demonstrate how these structural factors modulate the photoluminescence of coronene under high pressure. Combining high-pressure single-crystal X-ray diffraction, Raman spectroscopy, optical spectroscopy, and density functional theory calculations, we establish a relationship between distinct structural changes and the evolution of competing emissive states. Our results reveal that crystal polymorphism modifies the balance between free-exciton (FE) and self-trapped-exciton (STE) emission, while pressure-induced molecular bending is associated with a nonmonotonic evolution of STE emission. As intermolecular distances shorten, enhanced intermolecular electronic interactions give rise to excimer-related emission, introducing an additional emissive pathway. Although pressure-dependent optical properties of coronene have been linked to changes in crystal packing, our findings highlight that the optical response of a molecular solid is not governed by molecular deformation or crystal packing alone, but emerges from their interplay with intermolecular electronic coupling. By directly resolving molecular bending alongside changes in excited-state emission, this work provides insight into how distinct structural degrees of freedom can reshape the photophysical behavior of π-conjugated molecular solids.

title: Linear monitoring-feedback Model for Linearized gravity
summary: Whether gravity has quantum degrees of freedom is a question of fundamental importance. We formulate a linear monitoring-feedback framework for gravitational interactions that includes local classical-record models of semiclassical gravity and, when quantum resources are supplied in correlated ancilla inputs, can reproduce linearized quantum-gravity dynamics. Auxiliary systems monitor the positions of massive bodies, and their records are fed back through a chosen gravitational response kernel. At the level of linear input-output theory, this construction makes the deterministic response explicit while exposing the force noise and correlations associated with the auxiliary sector. We organize the allowed ancilla correlations into three regimes. In Regime-I, independent ancillas have unsqueezed, uncorrelated sensing and back-action quadratures. A single object then has a minimum classical-gravity noise (CGN), S_F^min = 2 hbar M Omega_SN^2, where Omega_SN is the Schrodinger-Newton frequency set by the microscopic mass distribution. In Regime-II, arbitrary local sensing--back-action correlations are allowed, but the ancillas associated with different objects remain independent. The single-object CGN is then unrestricted, while the joint force-noise matrix obeys a determinant bound that is equivalent to the local classical-channel/no-entanglement bound. In Regime-III, cross-object correlations and a common nonlocal mediator are allowed. The commuting force noises can then be jointly squeezed, entanglement between the masses can occur, and--with a suitable retarded response and input state--the monitoring-feedback system can reproduce the noise and commutators of linearized quantum gravity, including non-Markovian quantum fluctuations.

title: Tunable Valley Filtering and Splitting via Gate Control in Wrinkled Graphene
summary: We investigate the use of strain-induced wrinkles in graphene nanoribbons to achieve tunable valley filtering and splitting, crucial for advancing valleytronic devices. By combining tight-binding simulations, strain tensor analysis, and quantum transport calculations, we explicitly demonstrate that wrinkle-induced pseudomagnetic fields facilitate current splitting and valley-selective filtering in folded graphene nanoribbons based on wrinkle parameters like height, strain spreading/deformation and wrinkle orientation (tilt angle). Moreover, we show that the application of a top-gate voltage provides dynamic control over valley splitting, allowing a continuous transition from well-separated valley currents to valley merging as the gate voltage increases. In other parameter regimes, valley filtering arises from an initial current-splitting mechanism, exhibiting a clear gate-controlled transition between distinct transport behaviors. Our results offer new insights into strain-engineered valley transport and suggest a promising pathway toward practical graphene-based valleytronic devices.

title: Quantum kinetic uncertainty relations: Role of coherence in current fluctuation bounds
summary: We present a comparative analysis of three quantum versions of the kinetic uncertainty relation (KUR), which incorporate coherence-dependent corrections to the classical bound. Using a three-level maser heat engine as a paradigmatic quantum thermal machine, we identify the operating regimes in which each formulation provides the tightest constraint on current fluctuations. We further identify tighter, model-specific bounds for two of these formulations, provide numerical support for both, and establish one of them analytically. Introducing ground-state degeneracy, we then demonstrate that noise-induced coherence provides a tunable resource for relocating, enhancing, or suppressing violations of the standard KUR without requiring an additional coherent drive. In particular, it enables violations in regimes where the three-level engine satisfies the classical bound. Our results clarify how distinct quantum KURs account for coherence and constrain the precision of quantum thermal machines.

title: Exponential Lower Bounds for the Spherically Averaged Density of Atoms
summary: We study the asymptotic behavior of the spherically averaged density $\widetilde ρ$ for fermionic bound states of the $N$-electron atomic Hamiltonian $H_{N,Z}$ with nuclear charge $Z$. For the density associated with an eigenfunction satisfying $H_{N,Z}ψ=Eψ$, we show that if the energy $E$ is below the bottom of the essential spectrum $Σ:=\inf\mathop{\rm ess.spec} (H_{N,Z})$, then \[ \lim_{r\to\infty}\frac{\ln \widetilde ρ(r)}{r} =\lim_{r\to\infty}\frac{d}{dr}{\ln \widetildeρ(r)} =-2α_0, \] with $α_0=\sup\{α\ge 0\colon e^{2αr}\widetilde ρ\in L^1(\mathbb{R_+},r^2dr)\}$. The same is true at threshold in certain cases. Moreover, we prove $α_0^2=Σ-E$ for the ground states of $H_{3,Z}$ with sufficiently large $Z$.

title: Edge spin generalization for quantum Hall Laughlin droplets with elliptic shapes
summary: It is known that quasiparticles in the bulk of quantum Hall systems possess an emergent spin, which satisfies a spin-statistics relation. Recent results show that this spin can fractionalize: a quasiparticle spin in the bulk induces an opposite edge spin on the boundary. So far, the edge spin has only been studied in the simplest possible geometries, where the boundary is either circular or straight, without considering that a generic confining potential could give the droplet a non-symmetric shape. Yet, the value of the edge spin is not dictated by symmetry, but by topology: it is expected that the specific shape of the edge should not matter. In this work, we therefore generalize the edge spin to elliptically shaped droplets. We consider two different generalizations of the edge spin and test them on a family of elliptic Laughlin states introduced in the present work. The first, most straightforward, generalization is based on the properties of the single-particle orbitals for the elliptic confining potential. We show that this proposal applies to non-interacting states. The second proposal is based on the emergent properties of the quantum fluid. We show that this proposal also applies to interacting states, making it the suitable definition of the edge spin in the elliptic case. Our work demonstrates that it is possible to define an edge spin for Laughlin fluids with a non-trivial shape.

title: Dopant-vacancy complexes as single-photon-emitter candidates in monolayer silicon carbide: radiative and nonradiative decay
summary: Solid-state color centers have emerged as promising single-photon sources (SPSs). In particular, color centers in two-dimensional (2D) materials combine high photon brightness with scalable fabrication and ease of integration, offering a versatile platform for quantum information technologies. Realizing high-efficiency SPSs, however, requires strong radiative emission and negligible nonradiative decay. Using first-principles calculations, we assess radiative and nonradiative decay in dopant-vacancy complexes XSiVC (X = N, O, P, and S) in monolayer silicon carbide. All four defects exhibit stable neutral charge states and inter-defect optical transitions. Among them, PSiVC emerges as the leading single-photon-emitter candidate, combining rapid radiative decay with negligible nonradiative decay and a near-unity quantum yield within the modeled channels. By contrast, multiphonon decay limits the quantum yield of NSiVC despite its high Debye-Waller factor. Hyperfine tensors provide characteristic signatures for identifying the spin-active centers. Beyond identifying promising candidates, these results establish a joint radiative-nonradiative screening strategy and provide theoretical guidance for the rational design of color centers as solid-state SPSs.

title: Quantum Data Processing Unit for Neutral-Atom Quantum Computers
summary: Quantum computers need real-time classical processing to convert measurement data into feedback within device-specific timing constraints. We introduce the quantum data processing unit (QDPU), an architecture between a quantum device and its controller. Its core is a machine-learned quantum data model (QDM), adapted to the measurement response and noise characteristics of the device. We implement an FPGA pipeline for neutral-atom array assembly that performs occupancy detection and rearrangement scheduling in FPGA logic. One calibrated matched-filter lane classifies a $50\times50$ array in 12.5 $μ$s. An atom-loss model using a software reference planner evaluates a $35\times35$ target with a 60 s trap lifetime and 0.1% loss per moved atom. Removing an assumed 150 ms host round trip raises the predicted assembly success from 8% to 85% and reduces the wall-clock time per successful assembly from 19 s to 0.16 s. A GPU-based outer loop is proposed for refitting model parameters between runs. Its NVQLink transport is measured on the board: over 10 GbE to an NVIDIA DGX Spark, the median FPGA-to-host-to-FPGA round trip is 2.74 $μ$s for 128-byte messages forwarded by a CPU core. A separate 12-bit learned qLDPC kernel is placed and routed for the same FPGA target, with a derived latency of 0.84 ms per round for a $[[1122,148]]$ lifted-product code under code-capacity noise. A quantised GraphMP ranking kernel for the same code runs on the board with a median host-to-FPGA-to-host latency of 50.5 $μ$s with one shot in flight, excluding host-side BP+OSD post-processing. Together, these implementations illustrate a shared architecture with workload-specific models and timing requirements.

title: Charge-tunable acoustic surface plasmons in topological nodal-line semimetals
summary: Topological nodal-line semimetals host drumhead surface states, carrying a large surface density of states. We show that these states support an acoustic surface plasmon, whose velocity is strongly enhanced by the Coulomb interaction. At sufficiently small wavevectors, the mode lies above the surface particle-hole continuum and below both mixed surface-bulk absorption thresholds, leaving bulk particle-hole creation as the leading damping channel. Near drumhead depletion, the dispersion is highly sensitive to the surface charge, which suggests applications of plasmon spectroscopy of nodal-line semimetals to sensing technologies.

title: Correlation functions of the Lieb--Liniger Bose gas in equilibrium states: a microscopic approach to space-time asymptotics
summary: We develop an approximation-free approach to the analysis of form-factor series for the correlation functions of quantum integrable models in the thermodynamic limit and in equilibrium states described by a class of stationary density matrices. This allows us to obtain the long-time, large-distance asymptotics of the correlation functions in thermal equilibrium and in stationary states after a quench, including such states that can be described by generalized Gibbs ensembles. Our approach will be exemplified with the Lieb--Liniger Bose gas or non-linear Schrödinger model. It applies to the correlation functions of all local operators. For the two-point functions of particle-density or particle-current density operators our findings confirm the phenomenological predictions based on generalised hydrodynamics. We extract as well the long-time, large-distance asymptotics of a field- conjugated field correlation function. At present its behaviour is outside the reach of any heuristic method. It is governed by a novel non-linear integral equation that depends on space and time.

title: Two correlation scales in homogeneous density-matrix functionals: the Müller logarithm and the sharp Csányi--Arias asymptotics
summary:
We resolve the exact high-density correlation scales and coefficients of the three-dimensional translation-invariant, spin-symmetric Müller and Csányi--Arias corrected Hartree--Fock (CHF) functionals, settling long-standing numerical observations of Müller overcorrelation and apparently vanishing CHF correlation. In Hartree units, for fixed spin multiplicity $q$ and Fermi momentum $k=(6π^2ρ/q)^{1/3}$, their gains per particle over the filled Fermi sea satisfy \[
  D_{\rm M}(k)=\frac{3}{4π^2}\log k+O(1),\qquad
  D_{\rm CHF}(k)=12e^{-1/2-π^2/8}
  k^2e^{-π^{3/2}\sqrt{k}}(1+o(1)). \] The Müller proof retains the occupation cap and identifies the factor-of-two cancellation between exchange defect and energy gain. For periodic Müller jellium, convexity and translation--spin averaging allow a global minimizer to be chosen invariant and identify the unrestricted thermodynamic energy with the homogeneous spin-symmetric value. The CHF upper bound follows from a deterministic comparison built from the explicit Hartree--Fock dispersion, combining a full Birman--Schwinger bound with one-sided norms and completion of the square; a number-preserving trial state provides the matching lower bound, and the retained remainder yields weighted $L^2$ convergence of the occupation defect without analyzing the self-consistent gap. We also prove existence for both functionals and uniqueness of the CHF minimizer. Relative to the unpolarized quantum high-density benchmark, Müller has a larger logarithmic coefficient, providing quantitative evidence for the conjectured Müller lower-bound property, whereas CHF misses the logarithmic scale altogether. The quantum benchmark is not used in either functional proof.

title: Phase-resolved spin-orbit exciton transfer with dressed quantum encodings
summary: A quantum simulation of a material runs on a register much smaller than the electronic problem behind it, and the map between the two decides what a measured correlation means. We study this map for spin--orbit exciton transfer across an Ir--Ir bond of a LiIrF$_6$-derived model. Exact references show that a bare product-state encoding has an amplitude floor above a 0.02 state tolerance at sampled times, whereas a polar-dressed encoding lowers the ten-window projected error from 0.320 to $3.54\times10^{-4}$. Three-CZ axial and two-CZ transverse circuits, run on IBM Kingston in eight acquisitions with 1.6 million shots, resolve population transfer together with both quadratures of the intersite coherence. Raw half-transfer Bell-projector scores reach 0.935 in two independent acquisitions, and on a second bond a coherent arm with lower bound 0.871 is separated from a matched dephased control. Across 2,520 model points, adaptive spectral encodings meet fixed accuracy targets with explicit dimension costs.

title: Ultrafast Imaging Reveals Energy Transport Anisotropy Grows from Bulk to Monolayer Black Phosphorus
summary: Black phosphorus is an emerging low-dimensional semiconductor whose tunable band gap, high carrier mobility, and anisotropic transport make it attractive for directional energy transport in electronics and thermoelectrics. Using ultrafast stroboscopic optical scattering microscopy (stroboSCAT), we image spatiotemporal evolution of energy carriers with picosecond resolution, simultaneously resolving heat and charge transport in bulk black phosphorus and exciton transport in the monolayer. The in-plane armchair:zigzag anisotropy increases from 5.3:1 in the bulk to 6.7:1 in the monolayer, driven by enhanced armchair exciton diffusivity (45.5 cm$^2$/s) relative to bulk armchair charge carriers (16.5 cm$^2$/s). The monolayer anisotropy is smaller than the calculated exciton dispersion alone would suggest, which first-principles calculations attribute to preferential exciton-phonon scattering to large momenta along the zigzag direction. These directly measured, layer-resolved diffusivities identify armchair-aligned monolayers as the optimal geometry for directional transport and show that transport anisotropy cannot be inferred from band dispersion alone.

title: Fast forward-and-backward creation of non-equilibrium Gibbs state in driven dissipative quantum systems
summary: We present the fast-forward (FF) approach to adiabatic time evolution of an open dissipative quantum system within the framework of the Gorini-Kosaakowski-Sudarshan-Lindblad (GKSL) equation. Taking a harmonic oscillator (HO) and a quantum spin as prototype systems under a rapid change of the driving field and in contact with the heat reservoir, we reveal the protocol which creates the non-equilibrium Gibbs state. After preparing the Gibbs state under the fixed external field in advance, we begin to change adiabatically the field. To keep a quasi-adiabatic version of the Gibbs state as the solution of GKSL equation, we solve the inverse problem to obtain the non-adiabatic corrections both to Hamiltonian and to the dissipator. Then we apply the fast forward-and-backward (abbreviated as FF for convenience) time-rescaling, obtaining the FF variants of both Hamiltonian and detailed balance condition (DBC) among dissipative coefficients. The present scheme generates the time-periodic Gibbs state as if a limit-cycle solution of the innovated GKSL equation under the time-periodic driving field. Thanks to the FF variant of DBC, we see the energy conservation of power and heat current of the system, and reversibility of whole system including a reservoir. The requirement of positivity of the FF dissipative coefficients imposes a constraint on the speed of the FF driving. At low temperature, the upper speed limit of the FF periodic driving is found to be proportional to $\tildeβ^{-1/2}\exp(a\tildeβ)$ with $\tildeβ$ the scaled inverse temperature and $a$ the positive constant of $O(1)$.

title: Digitally-alloyed magnetic topological insulator nanostructures grown via stencil mask molecular beam epitaxy
summary: Magnetic topological insulator nanostructures are a promising platform for the realization of fault-tolerant quantum computation. For this, such nanostructures need to be embedded into the necessary superconducting architectures. In this study, we demonstrate a method for the growth of magnetic topological insulator nanostructures via molecular beam epitaxy, utilising digital alloying and defining their shapes in-situ by stencil mask technology. Cr-doped (Bi$_y$Sb$_{1-y}$)$_2$Te$_3$ micro- and nanometer-sized Hall bars are fabricated and the magneto-transport properties for various Cr doping amounts and different Hall bar dimensions are investigated at low temperatures. We find indications that the Fermi energy is located inside the bulk band gap, while disorder and charge puddles affect the transport behaviour. Furthermore, we investigate the magnetic properties and discuss the transition from ferromagnetic to paramagnetic behaviour.

title: The Thermodynamic Limit and the Landau degeneracy
summary: Usually, thermodynamic quantities are calculated by first regularizing the system in a confining box, which may have hard walls or periodic boundaries. One then studies the finite system and takes the thermodynamic limit by letting the box grow indefinitely. Here, we discuss a regularization scheme devised in the late 1980s [1] to study the thermodynamic equations of an anyon gas [2]. Instead of confining the system with walls, the method adds a smooth harmonic potential. Quantities are evaluated in its presence, and the potential is then gradually removed. A suitable prescription for taking this limit is needed to obtain meaningful thermodynamic results.

title: Testing correlated spin--orbit multiplets beyond excitation centroids
summary: Matching an excitation centroid does not establish the resolved structure of a correlated spin--orbit multiplet. Across eight embedded iridium and osmium compounds, ligand-active XMS-CASPT2 places the K$_2$OsCl$_6$ centroid within 0.5~meV of a RIXS maximum while splitting its nearly degenerate reference triplet by 2.54~meV, and matched OpenMolcas 26.10 controls retain the bare-anion sensitivities. Independent BAGEL calculations isolate contraction dependence in a three-state spin-free model: on the same reference, replacing SS--SR with MS--MR reduces the symmetry-defined E-block splitting from 0.448~meV to $4.67\times10^{-5}$~meV. Native reconstruction, reference symmetry, representation invariance, sensitivity controls and comparison with fitted spectral features or magnetic response provide an ordered validation procedure whose tests constrain different properties of the Hamiltonian.

title: Influence of interfacial roughness amplitude and periodicity on giant chiral asymmetry of domain wall mobility in epitaxial Cu/Pd/Co/Pd(111) films
summary: We investigate the influence of interfacial roughness amplitude and lateral periodicity on the chirality-dependent mobility of domain walls (DWs) in epitaxial Si(111)/Cu(2-7 nm)/Pd(3 nm)/Co(0.7 nm)/Pd(3 nm) heterostructures. By varying the Cu buffer layer thickness, we systematically modify the morphology of the magnetic interfaces while maintaining a constant composition and thickness of the Pd/Co/Pd trilayer. Scanning tunneling microscopy reveals that increasing the Cu thickness leads to the development of a hierarchical interfacial morphology characterized by increasing roughness amplitude and lateral periodicity. We observe a dramatic enhancement of the asymmetry between the velocities of DWs with opposite chirality in the creep regime, reaching a velocity ratio of approximately 50000 in the sample with a 7-nm-thick Cu buffer layer. This value exceeds by more than an order of magnitude the effective saturated asymmetry previously observed in Pd/Co/Pd structures with roughness controlled by the bottom Pd layer thickness. Despite comparable root-mean-square interface roughness in both series, the Cu-buffer-induced morphology exhibits a substantially larger characteristic lateral periodicity. We propose that the enhanced asymmetry originates from the different spatial organization of interfacial disorder, which modifies the pinning energy landscape and amplifies chirality-dependent thermally activated DW propagation. Our results suggest that engineering not only the amplitude but also the lateral spatial correlations of interfacial roughness provides an effective approach for controlling chiral DW dynamics in magnetic heterostructures.

title: Multitime Equilibration and Multitime Mpemba Effects
summary: Equilibration of a quantum state leaves open whether its response to later interventions has also equilibrated. We establish multitime equilibration for a continuous process on a fixed observation window, retaining the autonomous system--environment dynamics and all internal time differences. A finite-time mean-square bound controls the full continuous-process norm through the effective energy dimension and energy-gap correlations. A factorial temporal-order bound lifts fixed-sector convergence to the full process, while a process-visible spectral measure distinguishes mean-square from pointwise equilibration. This framework defines multitime Mpemba effects by comparing preparations relative to one stationary process. In a semicircle-spectrum model, a preparation filter changes the decay exponent from $3/2$ to $5/2$ in every fixed sector and in the summed norm, despite a larger initial distance. A fixed unitary control and terminal measurement exhibit the same exponent improvement in their output probabilities. Noncommuting baths and a many-body spin environment separate this all-sector mechanism from selective finite-time acceleration.

title: Quantized resistance limitations for graphene p-n junction devices
summary: Developing high-resistance quantized Hall resistance standards requires accessing values beyond the robust value seen in epitaxial graphene (R_{\mathrm{H}}=\ \frac{1}{2}\frac{h}{e^{2}}). This study evaluates the available parameter space of the coefficient of effective resistance across various epitaxial graphene p-n junction topologies, including rectangular, Corbino, and triangular layouts. Because mapping desired resistances to device configurations is mathematically degenerate, an automated Landauer-Büttiker Python solver was developed for all three topologies and was validated by cryogenic multi-terminal transport measurements and LTspice simulations. By analyzing the Shannon entropy of available states, it is found that rectangular checkerboards maximize topological complexity and tunable outputs, whereas Corbino geometries exhibit highly constrained resistance availabilities.

title: Group classification of a class of generalized Korteweg-de Vries equations
summary: Applying the method of furcate splitting, we carry out the complete group classification of a class of generalized Korteweg-de Vries equations. This class includes the Korteweg-de Vries, modified Korteweg-de Vries and Harry Dym equations, as well as the Rosenau-Hyman compacton equations. The equivalence group of the class is computed in two independent ways, by the advanced version of the direct method and by the megaideal-based version of the algebraic method. As a by-product, we construct the automorphism group of the equivalence algebra and all its megaideals, whose number is infinite. We also find all additional point equivalences between the classification cases. The maximal Lie invariance algebras of equations from the class are of dimensions from two to five, and all the corresponding Lie-symmetry extensions are regular except those for the equations similar to the Harry Dym equation, which are singular and are the only ones of the maximal dimension five. Finally, we classify the conservation laws of equations from the class with characteristics of nonpositive order.

title: Transfer-Matrix Calculus for Infinite Matrix Product States
summary: Long-range interactions, from the Coulomb repulsion between electrons to the power-law interactions of trapped ions and Rydberg atoms, are widespread in quantum many-body physics. For infinite systems, however, MPS algorithms, the standard classical reference in one dimension, conventionally rely on a computational compromise: replacing these interactions by fitted sums of exponentials. We develop transfer-matrix calculus (TMC), a unified framework for deriving infinite-MPS algorithms. In TMC, an interaction is written as a function of the transfer matrix, and one set of contraction rules then yields the effective Hamiltonians of DMRG and VUMPS, the tangent-space excitation action, and the energy variance, without an MPO. Long-range interactions thus enter with their prescribed distance dependence. For the half-filled lattice Coulomb chain with a $1/d$ interaction of strength $V$, theory predicts CDW order for all $V>0$, but at weak coupling this order is too weak for earlier numerics to resolve. Using TMC, we obtain infinite-MPS ground states at $V=2$ directly in the thermodynamic limit, with an energy variance per site of $2\times10^{-10}$. Our data, extrapolated to zero energy variance, indicate a small nonzero CDW amplitude, $m_0=0.002213(14)$, consistent with this prediction. The complete $V=2$ optimization workflow across the full series of bond dimensions takes less than a day on a single AMD MI250X GPU die. For an exactly solvable long-range hopping model, TMC reproduces the nonanalytic $|k|$ cusp of the one-particle dispersion that any fixed finite sum of decaying exponentials rounds off. We also use TMC to optimize first-quantized MPS directly in the thermodynamic limit. For half-filled free fermions, our entanglement entropy data show scaling consistent with central charge $c=1$ over the studied bond dimensions, as for second-quantized MPS.

title: Correlating orbital order and photovoltaic effect in Layered Ruddlesden-Popper Pr0.5Ca1.5MnO4 and PrCa2Mn2O7
summary: The understanding of growth and structure-property relations of epitaxial thin films of layered Ruddlesden-Popper perovskite oxides open up new pathways to tune correlated electron properties and to fabricate new types of correlated electron junctions, such as e.g. photovoltaic devices. In particular, the layered Ruddlesden-Popper systems Pr$_0.5$Ca$_1.5$MnO$_4$ and PrCa$_2$Mn$_2$O$_7$ at half doping exhibit much higher transition temperatures for the formation of charge and orbital ordered phases of $T_c$ = 320 K and $T_c$ up to 370 K, respectively, compared to the half doped non-layered system Pr$_{1-x}$Ca$_{x}$MnO$_3$ (PCMO) with $T_c$ = 240 K. Here, we demonstrate the successful growth of epitaxial PrCa$_2$Mn$_2$O$_7$ thin films by ion beam sputtering and compare electric transport, optical absorbance, electronic bandstructure and photovoltaic response with epitaxial Pr$_0.5$Ca$_1.5$MnO$_4$, both deposited on (Nb:)SrTiO$_3$ (110) substrates. An enhanced density of Ruddlesden-Popper type of stacking faults is identified as a relaxation channel for misfit strain in PrCa$_2$Mn$_2$O$_7$ and seems to be the origin for the reduced $T_c$ = 320 K and the reduced spatial coherence of charge and orbital order in comparison to Pr$_0.5$Ca$_1.5$MnO$_4$. Since the onset of the hot polaron photovoltaic effect is correlated to the formation of charge and orbital ordering, the comparative study of temperature dependent electric transport and photovoltaic response gives insights into the different role of strain and strain relaxation related defects on photo-electric properties.

title: Tight Quantum Query Bounds for Collision Finding over Arbitrary Bounded Types
summary:
We determine the bounded-error quantum query complexity of finding one $r$-collision in an $N$-input function of prescribed type, which specifies all equality-class sizes. For every fixed maximum class size and collision order, we give a tight bound as the maximum of scales determined by the numbers of classes of size at least $2,\ldots,r$. The lower bound holds for a uniformly random function of that type, and a matching algorithm succeeds on every such function. No intermediate class size is required to occur, and every feasible output alphabet is allowed.
  The characterization connects the abundant-collision regime associated with set equality to the sparse-target regime of $k$-distinctness. In particular, finding the unique $(k+1)$-collision in type $(k^n,k+1)$ has complexity $Θ_k(N^{3/4-1/[4(2^{k+1}-1)]})$, where $N=kn+k+1$, resolving an open problem of Belovs.
  For the lower bound, we introduce a filtered compressed permutation oracle that projects onto a harmonic database subspace after each complete function query. Its $O(T/N)$ comparison error over $T$ queries overcomes the square-root limitation of the unfiltered process. Hidden capacity extensions and moment estimates retain the populations at each intermediate collision order. Matching upper bounds use sampled collision lists and colored adaptive learning graphs, with a coherent decision-to-search conversion that avoids logarithmic overhead. We also give an alternative nested quantum-walk algorithm for three-collision search, matching the bound up to polylogarithmic factors.

title: Symmetry induced spin splitting of topological surface states at equal carrier density
summary: Surface states are among the most striking consequences of band inversion in topological materials. In magnetotransport of three-dimensional topological insulators, the typical signature of surface state transport is a quantized Hall conductance with nontrivial sequences of integer filling factors, varying with the total carrier density. For two independent Dirac carriers, one expects Hall plateaus only at odd-integer filling factors. In this work, we report the observation of symmetry induced spin splitting in magnetotransport experiments on a dual-gate three-dimensional topological insulator device based on HgTe. In the topological surface state regime, we observe Hall plateaus at both odd and even integers when we gate the device symmetrically, i.e., with equal density at the top and bottom. This phenomenon originates in structural inversion symmetry, which remarkably induces a spin splitting and forces the eigenstates to be symmetric and antisymmetric linear combinations of the top and bottom surface states. This is in contrast with two-dimensional systems, where spin splitting is caused by absence of inversion symmetry. We interpret the experimental observations with a perturbative model using isoparity eigenstates, the conserved quantum number associated with structural inversion. The result demonstrates that the picture where the top and bottom states are treated as independent Dirac carriers is not valid when the carrier density is symmetric.

title: Correlation functions of the Lieb--Liniger Bose gas in equilibrium states: a microscopic approach to space-time asymptotics
summary: We develop an approximation-free approach to the analysis of form-factor series for the correlation functions of quantum integrable models in the thermodynamic limit and in equilibrium states described by a class of stationary density matrices. This allows us to obtain the long-time, large-distance asymptotics of the correlation functions in thermal equilibrium and in stationary states after a quench, including such states that can be described by generalized Gibbs ensembles. Our approach will be exemplified with the Lieb--Liniger Bose gas or non-linear Schrödinger model. It applies to the correlation functions of all local operators. For the two-point functions of particle-density or particle-current density operators our findings confirm the phenomenological predictions based on generalised hydrodynamics. We extract as well the long-time, large-distance asymptotics of a field- conjugated field correlation function. At present its behaviour is outside the reach of any heuristic method. It is governed by a novel non-linear integral equation that depends on space and time.

title: Regularized Neural Quantum States for Heisenberg Magnets
summary: We introduce an approach to solving locally ordered quantum spin systems using neural network quantum states. First, our approach rests on choosing a spin basis constructed from the magnetic texture of a classical or quantum reference state. Second, the method improves convergence and suppresses parameter-space drift through a regularized Riemannian gradient descent adapted to the quantum state geometry of the variational state manifold. Combining these techniques enables stable ground-state calculations for two- and three-dimensional chiral spin systems with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions. The resulting variational ground-state energies are competitive with those of high-fidelity density matrix renormalization group calculations and, for periodic and layered geometries, provide significantly tighter upper bounds on the ground-state energy.

title: Epitaxial integration of GaN $μ$-platelets and thin films on metallic TiN using a hybrid approach
summary: We demonstrate the synthesis of epitaxial, self-organized GaN $μ$-platelets on metallic TiN thin films. To this end, we first nucleate self-assembled GaN nanowires with number densities between 0.01 to 300 $μm^{-2}$ by molecular beam epitaxy. Subsequent overgrowth of these seed nanowires by metal-organic vapor phase epitaxy yields GaN $μ$-platelets with corresponding number densities. The platelets exhibit N-polarity and form an ohmic contact to the metallic TiN substrate. By adjusting the growth conditions during the metal-organic vapor phase epitaxy, particularly the carrier gas and precursor ratio, the morphology of the GaN can be controlled across a broad range. Growth under N$_{2}$ carrier gas and with a 1:1 NH$_{3}$/trimethylgallium precursor flow ratio results in platelet ensembles with broad diameter and height distributions. In contrast, employing an N$_{2}$/H$_{2}$ carrier gas mixture promotes the formation of more homogeneous ensembles with narrower size distributions around a diameter of $\approx$2 $μm$. Finally, N-rich growth conditions under H$_{2}$ carrier gas enhance lateral growth, leading to the formation of coalesced GaN layers. GaN grown under these latter conditions exhibits strong near-band-edge emission, accompanied by only weak deep-level luminescence at room temperature.

title: No universal LOCC entanglement purification
summary: Entanglement purification aims to obtain high-fidelity entangled states from noisy entangled states. This task becomes particularly challenging when the available input states are finite in number, only partially characterized, and may not be identical. Whether there exists a universal purification protocol applicable to such inputs has therefore been a longstanding question. This motivates the study of universal $n$-to-$1$ entanglement purification. Although no such LOCC protocol exists for the full set of two-qubit entangled states, it has remained open whether this no-go result extends to higher-dimensional bipartite states and multipartite states. In this work, we resolve this question by proving that, for any fixed finite local dimensions, no $n$-to-$1$ LOCC protocol is universal for all bipartite entangled states or all multipartite entangled states. We further show that the bipartite and multipartite no-go results persist under several natural extensions and establish an analogous no-go theorem for coherence purification under strictly incoherent operations.

title: Topological Hybridization Gaps from Molecular Orbitals Coupled to Dirac Fermions
summary: A magnetically gapped topological-insulator surface carries a half-quantized Hall response. We show that hybridizing the surface Dirac fermions with a flat band of chiral orbitals adds an integer to it: spin-momentum locking forces the hybridization to wind around the band-crossing ring, opening a topological gap. For orbitals with total angular momentum $j$, rotational symmetry fixes the surface Hall conductivity to $je^2/h$, with the sign set by the Dirac branch crossed and independent of the sign of the Dirac mass. The result survives crystal-field quenching of the orbital moment, with the winding then set by interference between hybridization pathways. First-principles calculations for a monolayer of nitric oxide adsorbed on Bi$_2$Se$_3$ predict a $\sim 20$ meV hybridization gap and an intrinsic surface Hall conductivity of $\frac{3}{2}e^2/h$, identifying molecular orbital angular momentum as a handle on surface topology.

title: All coupling Anderson localization in the quantum kicked rotor model
summary: In this paper, we study $$\mathscr{H}=λΔ+\tanπ(θ+n^2α)δ_{n,n'},\ n\in\Bbb Z$$ and prove its Anderson localization for all $λ>0$ and Lebesgue almost every (a.e.) $(α, θ)\in\Bbb T^2$. This conforms in the full measure sense the main assumption of Fishman-Grempel-Prange [{\it Phys. Rev. Lett.} 49(8), 509--512 (1982)] in the study of the quantum suppression of chaos: The pseudo-randomness of the sequence $\{\tanπ(θ+n^2α)\}_{n\in\Bbb Z}$ (for $α\in\Bbb T\setminus \Bbb Q$) should result in all coupling Anderson localization for $H$ similar to that for the one-dimensional Anderson model. Our proof is based on nonperturbative Green's function estimates approach using Cayley transform, quadratic Weyl sum estimate and Rellich function analysis.

title: Fibonacci Non-Abelian Quantum Hall States with Pair Structure - a classification of chiral 2-cluster many-body wave-functions
summary: Fibonacci anyons support universal topological quantum computation. They have been proposed to emerge in fractional quantum Hall (FQH) systems, such as the filling-fraction $ν=\tfrac{2}{3}$ state described by an effective $SU(3)_2$ Chern-Simons theory, and the $ν=\tfrac{2}{5}$ state with a $3$-cluster structure (an $n$-cluster structure means that $n$-electron bound states form a Laughlin-type wave function of the form $(z^{(n)}_i-z^{(n)}_j)^m$). In this work, we systematically classify FQH wave functions $P(z_1,\ldots,z_N)$ in the $N\rightarrow\infty$ limit, through a generalized pattern of zeros (gPOZ) approach, where the wave function is determined by the leading order of zero along with the accompanying leading polynomial that develops as successive number of $z_i$'s are brought together. Within this approach, we obtain a $(ν,h,c)$-classification of wave functions with a $2$-cluster (pair) structure. Among these wave functions, those with $(h,c) = (\tfrac12,\tfrac12)$, $(\tfrac32,\tfrac{7}{10})$, $(3,\tfrac45)$ correspond to gapped FQH states with filling fraction $ν$ and edge-state chiral central charge $c+1$, while others with $c<0$ may be gapless. We find that even a $2$-cluster structure can give rise to Fibonacci statistics, for $(ν,h,c) = (\tfrac14,\tfrac32,\tfrac{7}{10})$, corresponding to the $(5,4)$ minimal model, and for $(ν,h,c) = (\tfrac17,3,\tfrac45)$, corresponding to the $(6,5)$ minimal model. We further construct an ideal $4$-body Hamiltonian whose ground state is the $(\tfrac14,\tfrac32,\tfrac{7}{10})$ state.

title: A Machine-learning-aided Workflow for Sampling Small Polaron Dynamics in Energy Materials
summary:
One of the defining characteristics of most energy materials, used as e.g.~battery electrodes, photovoltaics, or photocatalysts, is their ability conduct charges such as electrons and holes. The exact mechanism of this conductivity depends on the material, but is often dominated by the existence of mobile small polarons, i.e.~electrons or holes strongly localised through the polarisation of their environment. Computationally, small polarons can be treated with reasonably accuracy through the use of self-interaction corrected or hybrid density functional theory (DFT) together with local geometry optimisation. Similar approaches can be employed to determine the energy barriers to movement of the polarons through hopping. Unfortunately, realistic energy materials tend have very large numbers of symmetry inequivalent polaronic configurations and correspondingly large numbers of hopping barriers, making them hard to tackle explicitly.
  In this work we therefore extend the computational reach of DFT calculations with machine-learned (ML) surrogate models, which then feed into a kinetic model to quantitatively estimate the conductivity of a battery anode material (Li$_4$Ti$_5$O$_12$ or LTO) at realistic, defected conditions. We calculate the conductivity at room temperature to be 6.7 $\times$ 10$^{-3}$ S/cm which lies well in the experimental range. To this end, we only needed a total of 154 polaron barrier calculations, out of 3649 symmetry inequivalent ones, achieving an over 20-fold increase of computational efficiency. Overall, our work demonstrates how DFT-trained ML surrogates can be used to quantitatively and efficiently sample the dynamics of small polarons in energy materials.

title: Local gluing classification and bulk-locked clock rings for $\mathbb{Z}_N$ models on a Klein bottle
comment: 15 pages, 4 figures; supporting code and data included as ancillary material
summary: We classify local reflection gluings of the $\mathbb{Z}_N$ plaquette model on lattice Klein bottles and solve the obstructed literal seam. Within the monomial far-corner ansatz, all commuting gluings form a family labelled by a unit $u$ of $\mathbb{Z}_N$. They exist for every $N$ at even seam length and, at odd length, exactly when $-1$ is a square modulo $N$. We determine the anyon transport, including exchange seams with $P^2=C$ for charge conjugation $C$, and the relation phases that distinguish an unfrustrated code from a commuting but frustrated Hamiltonian. For the literal gluing, the $2L_x$ noncommuting plaquettes form self-dual clock rings whose sectors are locked by the bulk. This gives an exact reduction of the spectrum to clock-ring spectra, closed-form ring ground energies for $N=2,4$, and a closed-form ground-state degeneracy. We further determine twisted-coefficient homology on the stated surface domains and compare it with logical modules on registered lattice grids; composite dimensions need not give squares of cyclic groups. Dressed-isometry gates and monodromy are reported with their finite-grid scope. Finally, the qudit Gottesman--Knill theorem bounds the computational interpretation: Clifford deformations and Weyl measurements with stabilizer inputs and no external magic states cannot supply a non-stabilizer resource. Charge-conjugation measurements that do supply such states lie outside this operation model. The new results concern explicit seam classification, phase-sensitive consistency and bulk-locked spectra, not a new general no-go theorem or a universal computing architecture.

title: Topological phase diagram of an extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model with negative coupling
summary: Recently, an extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model with three atoms per unit cell has been experimentally realized in perovskite exciton-polariton micropillars. A distinctive feature of this system is that the second and third bands undergo a topological transition through a band crossing at the wave vector $k=0$, associated with a negative coupling. In this work, we analytically determine the phase diagram of the model as a function of the on-site energy splitting and the ratio of intercell to intracell hopping amplitudes. We identify seven regions in this lane, with four distinct topological phases, characterized by different Zak phases of the three bands. Our results provide a useful theoretical framework for interpreting existing experiments and serve as a guide for future experimental investigations of this system.

title: Restoring Consistency with Poynting's Theorem in Numerical MHD and RMHD
summary: For perfectly conducting plasmas, Poynting's theorem states that the time rate of change of electromagnetic energy density equals the negative of the divergence of the Poynting flux. To the best of our knowledge, this involutive theorem has never been mimetically incorporated in codes. We show that there is an inconsistency in MHD and RMHD codes that evolve face-centered magnetic fields in globally-divergence-free fashion. This is because the face-centered flux of energy density, which incorporates a Poynting vector, is evaluated using one-dimensional Riemann solvers that are applied at face-centers. However, the face-centered magnetic fields are evolved according to edge-centered electric fields that come from two-dimensional Riemann solvers that are applied to the edges of a zone. While edge-centered electric fields are used to evolve the magnetic field, they have no influence on the face-centered Poynting flux. For situations where the magnetic energy is much larger than the thermal energy, this causes a negative pressure to be evaluated at the zone-centers. This paper restores consistency by using edge-centered variables to evaluate a face-centered Poynting flux. A simple accuracy-preserving correction is made to the face-centered flux of energy density. We show that it helps considerably in simulations that have very strong magnetic fields.

title: Analytic spread complexity in three-level systems and the spacing-ratio distribution
summary: The spread complexity characterizes the spreading of a quantum state over the Krylov basis and has been proposed to capture the correlations between energy levels. How such correlations manifest in the dynamics has been studied mainly numerically for large matrices. Here we consider three-level systems, the smallest setting with spacing correlations, and derive exact results for the spread complexity, the Krylov variance, and the Krylov entropy. At infinite temperature, the Krylov basis depends on the spectrum only through the ratio of consecutive level spacings, and the spectral variance enters only as an overall time scale. For Gaussian ensembles, these variables are statistically independent, and the averaged spread complexity and variance reduce to one-dimensional integrals over the spacing-ratio distribution encoding the level statistics. We establish universal late-time values of the complexity and variance, and an algebraic relaxation with exponents set by the Dyson index. We also outline the extension to $d$ levels, with the ensemble-averaged spread complexity expressed as a $(d-2)$-dimensional integral over the joint distribution of consecutive spacing ratios.

title: Pressure dependent DFT study of mechanical, thermal, electronic, magnetic, and optical properties of EuCd2As2: a magnetic semimetal
summary: We present a comprehensive spin-polarized density functional theory (DFT) investigation of the pressure-dependent physical properties of EuCd2As2, a magnetically and topologically rich compound with potential applications in spintronics and optoelectronics technologies. We have investigated the structural, mechanical, thermophysical, acoustic, electronic, magnetic, and optical properties of this material at pressures of 0, 2, 4, 6, and 8 GPa. The calculated lattice parameters at zero pressure are in good agreement with experimental values. The mechanical stability of EuCd2As2 is maintained over the investigated pressure range. The elastic constants, bulk modulus, shear modulus, and Young's modulus are found to be tunable with applied pressure. The compound undergoes a brittle to ductile transition at higher pressures. The Debye temperature, melting temperature, and Grüneisen parameter are found to be strongly pressure-dependent. Phonon thermal conductivity has been evaluated. The electronic properties of EuCd2As2 were studied through band structure and density of states (DOS). The effect of pressure up to 8 GPa was investigated for the ferromagnetic (FM) phase. At 0 GPa, the calculated FM band structure exhibits no band gap at the Fermi level, which confirms the semimetallic nature of EuCd2As2. The net magnetic moment of 6.96 μ_B per unit cell was obtained for this compound indicating its potential for spintronics application. The optical properties, including the dielectric function, refractive index, absorption coefficient, optical conductivity, reflectivity, and loss function, are calculated. The calculated optical spectra indicate strong absorption in the visible and ultraviolet regions, suggesting that EuCd2As2 may have potential for optoelectronic applications.

title: Reference-Assisted Qutrit Control and Conditional One-Round Distillation in a Charge-4e Superconductor Model
comment: 13 pages; code and data included as ancillary files
summary: We formulate a charge-$4e$ parafermionic-vortex route to qutrit processing as a conditional theory with explicit operational assumptions. Sector preservation and same-label charge-conjugation covariance imply closure for every adaptive visible record. For charge-conjugation-invariant inputs, record probabilities are independent of the supported reference state; for arbitrary inputs, discarding the reference gives a population-weighted mixture of conjugate sector maps. We give a finite-depth stability bound for complete labelled instruments, including postselection and initial zero-sector contamination. A self-contained calculation reproduces the known dense single-qutrit closure of the registered Clifford-plus-Flip gate set. We also specify an abstract ternary CSS $[[11,1,5]]_3$ syndrome/recovery decoder: 243 classical representatives per CSS component correct all 3,609 Pauli errors of support weight at most two, and an exact integer dynamic program yields the full independent-Pauli logical enumerator. Its all-syndrome acceptance is distinct from the known $1/1728$ ideal acceptance of one-round strange-state Golay distillation. An accepted-run target-infidelity budget and a synthetic parameter protocol expose the remaining noise assumptions. Native charge-$4e$ syndrome extraction, material feasibility, a device threshold, and unconditional fault tolerance are not established.

title: Quantum melting and Pomeranchuk effect of zero-field Wigner solids
comment: Accepted for publication in npj Quantum Materials
summary: Wigner solids and crystals are many-body phases of matter in which repulsive interactions between the charge carriers cause them to freeze into a solid. How Wigner solids compete or cooperate with integer and fractional quantum Hall liquids has been a long-standing open question. Here, we investigate this question for zero-field, electron and hole Wigner solids in cadmium arsenide quantum wells. In the low temperature limit, our results are consistent with a recent theoretical model [A. P. Reddy and L. Fu, Phys. Rev. B 113, L161403 (2026)] that proposes that the quantum Hall liquid can become energetically favored over the solid at low integer filling factors. Going beyond the low-temperature limit, we observe a re-entrant solid that emerges from the quantum Hall liquid. We explain this observation by considering the role of spin entropy, in close analogy with the zero-field Pomeranchuk effect, but appearing here at finite fields. The competition between quantum Hall liquids and Wigner solids is thus governed by both energy and entropy terms, giving rise to rich phase stability diagrams that result from the interplay between topology and correlations.

title: Fast mixing and thermal phases from strong decay of correlations
summary: We show that a strong form of correlation decay in quantum Gibbs states has far-reaching dynamical consequences. For a smooth path of geometrically local commuting Hamiltonians whose Gibbs states satisfy strong decay of correlations, we construct $\mathrm{O}(1)$-time quasi-local Lindbladian evolutions exactly connecting these states in both directions, together with $\mathrm{O}(1)$-time quasi-local Hamiltonian evolutions exactly connecting their canonical purifications. These quasi-local connections strengthen previously known quantum-channel circuit constructions based on the decay of connected correlation functions [R. Ma, V. Khemani, and S. Sang, PRX Quantum 7, 033052 (2026)], which approximately connect states within the same phase but have depths that grow logarithmically with system size. Furthermore, if the Gibbs-state path contains a product state, we prove that the single-site Glauber dynamics has a $Ω(1)$ spectral gap independent of the system size throughout the path. This establishes Glauber-dynamics fast mixing for models that may violate the strong spatial mixing condition used in prior proofs, including (1) the $q$-state Potts model throughout the high-temperature phase for any $q$ and any finite dimension; (2) the Ising model with a longitudinal field at low temperature, with frustrating perturbations that destroy monotonicity of the dynamics; and (3) the three-dimensional $\mathbb{Z}_2$ lattice gauge theory at low temperatures comparing to a field perturbation, even though the model supports classical memories at intermediate temperatures. Intriguingly, we establish fast mixing of these classical Markov chains using tools from quantum physics like Lieb-Robinson bounds.

title: Probing Spatiotemporal Quantum Correlations with Two-Qubit Relaxometry
summary: Quantum impurities and spin qubits are powerful local probes of magnetic fluctuations, but conventional relaxometry reduces their information to a local relaxation rate at a single frequency. Building on advances in two-qubit sensing of spatial correlations, we show how two complementary protocols probe finite-time correlations in interacting quantum matter. Phase-cycled Bell-state relaxometry isolates the signed contribution of correlated relaxation to the joint ground-state population. To second order in the probe-environment coupling, the resulting population contrast measures a finite-time integral of the energy-ordered cross-correlator. In the longitudinal regime, XY8 covariance probes the complementary symmetrized cross-correlator within a tunable frequency window. For a gapless quantum spin chain, the signals reveal interaction-dependent algebraic scaling and ballistic propagation. Luttinger-liquid theory links sign changes as the qubit frequency is swept to the propagation time between the probes. It also predicts distinct spatial power laws for the Bell signal before the correlation front and at late times, when the sensing window resolves the qubit frequency. Matrix-product-state calculations for the spin chain test the pre-front scaling at zero and finite magnetization and extract the propagation velocity from Bell oscillations at zero magnetization. The probe coupling geometry determines which spin and momentum sectors contribute to the measured signals.

title: Making Plasticity Visible: A Case Study for High-Temperature Exposed Aluminum Alloy
summary: Understanding the onset of plastic deformation and the early development of strain localization is essential for characterizing material behavior and identifying failure-prone regions. However, these transitions are not always distinguishable from conventional full-field strain measurements. This study investigates a data- driven framework combining Digital Image Correlation (DIC) and Principal Component Analysis (PCA) to extract temporal and spatial deformation signatures during uniaxial tensile loading. The methodology is evaluated using AA6063-T5 aluminum alloy specimens in the as-received condition and following thermal exposure at 100~$^\circ$C, 200~$^\circ$C, and 300~$^\circ$C. PCA applied to sequential strain fields reveals a characteristic peak in the second principal component projection near the yielding transition, showing agreement with the conventional 0.2\% offset criterion across the investigated conditions. Furthermore, principal component maps extracted from high-temporal-resolution strain fields preceding this transition highlight localized deformation features associated with subsequent failure regions. These features are more clearly distinguishable than competing strain concentrations in the corresponding instantaneous strain maps. The results indicate that PCA-derived deformation signatures remain identifiable despite thermally induced variations in mechanical response. This approach demonstrates the potential of unsupervised dimensionality reduction for extracting physically interpretable information on plastic deformation and early strain localization from experimental full-field measurements.

title: Four-Sector Propagation-Trapping Decomposition and Inverse Design of Initial States in Grover-Coined Quantum Walks on Multiedge Path Graphs
comment: 12 pages, 2 figures, 1 table. Submitted to Physical Review A
summary: Controlling propagation and trapping through initial-state preparation requires an explicit relation between the initial amplitudes and the corresponding directional probabilities. We establish this relation for a discrete-time Grover-coined quantum walk on a multiedge path graph with even degree d = 2M, where M is at least 2, and two equal directional blocks. Each block of an arbitrary local state is expressed as its mean component plus a zero-sum deviation. The Grover coin performs a pure exchange of the two block means and reverses the sign of each zero-sum deviation. Together with the graph routing, this gives a unique orthogonal decomposition into four sectors: propagation in opposite directions and bounded trapping on either side of the launch vertex. We derive the four sector probabilities and solve the inverse problem, constructing initial states for any prescribed nonnegative probability quadruple that sums to unity. Explicit representatives are given for d = 4 and d = 6. Sector-resolved simulations reproduce the predicted motion, conservation of sector weights, and local probability additivity, including repeated spatial overlaps. We also derive the local Grover action for an arbitrary partition into blocks of possibly unequal sizes, explicitly describing how their means are redistributed while each zero-sum deviation remains within its block and changes sign. The framework provides direct control of propagation and trapping within one fixed graph and walk operator through the preparation of the initial state.

title: Narrow-Band Magnetism Allowed by Quantum Geometry: Altermagnetism and Beyond
comment: 5 pages, 3 figures in the main text, 20 pages, 17 figures in the Supplemental Material
summary: Quantum geometry plays a central role in shaping correlated phases in narrow bands, yet its influence on the competition between distinct magnetic orders, especially the emergence of altermagnetism, remains largely unexplored. To address this question, we study the quadrupole insulator model with strictly onsite generalized Hubbard-Kanamori interactions, in which both Néel antiferromagnetism and altermagnetism are symmetry-permitted. Depending on the parameters, the isolated narrow lowest band of the model can either be obstructed atomic with strong quantum geometry or trivial atomic with weak quantum geometry, while the dispersion is identical in the two cases. By partially filling the lowest band, our Hartree-Fock calculations show only conventional ferromagnetic phases for the weak quantum geometric case, while we find two collinear altermagnetic phases, as well as nematic phases, for the strong quantum geometric case. Such a dramatic difference can be understood by the distinct characters of the projected interaction: the projected interactions acquire sizable longer-range channels only for the strong quantum geometric case, while they are dominated by the on-site Hubbard channel in the weak quantum geometric case. These results establish the essential role of quantum geometry for altermagnetism to emerge from interacting narrow bands where crystalline symmetries cannot sufficiently constrain the magnetic order.

title: Local Quantum Metrology: Precision Limits for Observers in QFT
summary: How precisely can an observer estimate a parameter related to a quantum field? This question is answered for quantum-mechanical systems using the SLD--Bures--Fisher metric and the quantum Cramér--Rao bound. However, local algebras in relativistic quantum field theory are of type III: they carry no trace and normal states have no density matrices, so the SLD quantum Fisher information and the quantum Cramér--Rao bound cannot be defined in the usual way. We define the SLD (Bures) quantum Fisher information on arbitrary von Neumann algebras through Uhlmann's transition probability and prove a quantum Cramér--Rao bound for collective measurements. We also show that the bound is sharp, and equals the largest classical Fisher information obtainable by measurements in the region.

title: Theoretical exploration of ambient-pressure superconductivity in the bilayer nickelate: A strategy of atomic substitution for tuning chemical pressure
summary: The possibility of ambient-pressure superconductivity in $\mathrm{La_3Ni_2O_7}$ is theoretically explored via chemical substitution. Using first-principles and many-body calculations, we propose substituting $\mathrm{Ba}$ at the lanthanide site to exert chemical pressure, thereby mitigating the octahedral distortions that suppress superconductivity. Phonon calculations demonstrate the dynamical stability of the high-symmetry tetragonal phase in $\mathrm{La_{3-\it{x}}Ba_{\it{x}}Ni_2O_7}$ at a small doping ratio of $x \sim 0.15$. By applying the fluctuation exchange approximation to an effective model Hamiltonian derived from this stable structure, we calculate the Eliashberg eigenvalue $λ$ to evaluate the relative superconducting transition temperature $T_\mathrm{c}$ to existing unconventional superconductors. We conclude that $s_\pm$-wave superconductivity is likely to emerge, as the required $\mathrm{Ba}$ concentration ($x \sim 0.15$) is sufficiently small to minimize the detrimental suppression of superconductivity induced by hole doping.

title: Mapping the Phase Space of Cubic Chiral Semiconductors: High-Throughput Search,Stability, and Prototype Families
summary: Chiral crystals show unique electronic, magnetic, and optical characteristics that make them attractive for topological and spintronic applications. Nevertheless, the limited set of identified chiral semiconductors, especially those with cubic symmetry, has so far constrained their technological application. In this work, we perform a high-throughput computational search for semiconducting chiral compounds in the cubic space group $P4_332$ (No. 212). By integrating machine-learning techniques with density functional theory, we obtain 24\,227 cubic chiral structures containing up to five elements, and identify 368 thermodynamically stable semiconductors on the convex hull and 3\,048 within 50~meV/atom. We analyze their structural motifs, stability, and electronic band structures, highlighting recurring prototype families, several of which show intrinsic intermediate-band features. Our results substantially expand the known phase space of cubic chiral semiconductors and may guide future efforts in the discovery and design of chiral materials.

title: Hardware-aware sampling and QPU-informed Monte Carlo with quantum annealers
summary: We study how the physical representation of a logical model affects sampling by quantum annealers and its use in corrected Monte Carlo. The square-lattice Ising model provides controlled classical references. Fixed embeddings with one physical qubit per logical spin reach $36\times36$ spins. Comparisons with uniform two-qubit chains and mixed chain lengths show that matching mean energy leaves differences in magnetization and correlations. Extended-range conditional predictors improve the description of mixed embeddings, distinguishing their residual correlations from those of the tested uniform embeddings. Independent calibration checks and fixed-scale annealing scans show that temperature shifts alone do not determine distributional agreement. Normalized autoregressive models learned from QPU samples provide proposals with exact Metropolis--Hastings and multiple-try corrections on larger periodic lattices. These preserve the target distribution, although block updates alone relax critical magnetization slowly. Complementary direct-QPU updates reveal how block size and fitted-temperature correction affect acceptance and spin motion. Together, the results support prioritizing one-qubit representations and short uniform chains, while separating hardware sampling fidelity from the convergence of corrected Monte Carlo.

title: Probing Spatiotemporal Quantum Correlations with Two-Qubit Relaxometry
summary: Quantum impurities and spin qubits are powerful local probes of magnetic fluctuations, but conventional relaxometry reduces their information to a local relaxation rate at a single frequency. Building on advances in two-qubit sensing of spatial correlations, we show how two complementary protocols probe finite-time correlations in interacting quantum matter. Phase-cycled Bell-state relaxometry isolates the signed contribution of correlated relaxation to the joint ground-state population. To second order in the probe-environment coupling, the resulting population contrast measures a finite-time integral of the energy-ordered cross-correlator. In the longitudinal regime, XY8 covariance probes the complementary symmetrized cross-correlator within a tunable frequency window. For a gapless quantum spin chain, the signals reveal interaction-dependent algebraic scaling and ballistic propagation. Luttinger-liquid theory links sign changes as the qubit frequency is swept to the propagation time between the probes. It also predicts distinct spatial power laws for the Bell signal before the correlation front and at late times, when the sensing window resolves the qubit frequency. Matrix-product-state calculations for the spin chain test the pre-front scaling at zero and finite magnetization and extract the propagation velocity from Bell oscillations at zero magnetization. The probe coupling geometry determines which spin and momentum sectors contribute to the measured signals.

title: The cone of states over time: exact tests and convergent two-sided hierarchies
summary: A state over time (stote) pairs a state $ρ$ with a channel $\mathcal{E}$ as the Hermitian, generally non-positive operator $(ρ\otimes\mathbf{1})\star J_\mathcal{E}$. We study the convex cone $\widehat{\mathcal{Q}}$ generated by these operators. Our main result is a convergent outer semidefinite hierarchy with an explicit trace-norm Hausdorff bound on its trace-one slices.
